title: Precedent
description: One real building, as a record a checker can resolve. Until WP-11.1 an exemplar was a name with no locator: 482 exemplars across 164 style nodes, 410 distinct buildings, and not one carried a HABS number, a register reference or a link, so a reader could find Westover and a checker could resolve nothing. A precedent is the building itself -- shared by every node that names it (Stanley-Whitman House stands for three) -- with the archival references that locate it and, where the Historic American Buildings Survey wrote one, its written data quoted verbatim. Every URL records when it was read and by which route, because from this project's own container the Library of Congress answers 403 and only two routes reach past that (`oq/fetching-through-a-tier-the-proxy-denies`). A record carries `rights_evidence` and never a `license`: a licence is a conclusion a person draws, and the asset schema says why.

id.description: Stable, never reused, equal to the filename. A building that turns out to be misnamed gets a new record; the old one is kept and points forward.

name.description: The name the style node's exemplar uses, exactly. `build/check_assets.py` holds asset records to exemplar names, so this is the join key everything else hangs off.

text.description: The exemplar's own `location` string, exactly -- the asset checker reads it as half the query.

state.description: State, county or region, as the source writes it.

built.description: As the source states it: `1755-1759`, `c. 1726`. A string, because a single integer is a claim the sources rarely make.

altered.description: Later work that changed what a photograph or a survey shows -- Westover's wings rebuilt about 1900, Gunston Hall's 1949-52 restoration.

nodes.description: Every style node whose `exemplars` names this building. `build/check_precedents.py` holds the two directions to each other.

kind.description: What sort of locator this is. `habs` carries the survey number (VA-141); `loc-item` the Library's item id (va0433); `nrhp` the eight-digit reference; `state-register` the state's own file number; `institution` the owning body's own page. The id shape per kind is checked by build/check_precedents.py, not here, so this file stays self-contained.

title.description: The page's own title as the source gave it, so a dead link can still be searched for.

retrieved.description: ISO date the reference was read. A reference nobody read on a stated day was typed from memory, which is how a wrong id is laundered as a citation.

via.description: The route it was read by. Closed, because these are the only routes that reach the archives from this project's tiers (`oq/fetching-through-a-tier-the-proxy-denies`, ruled 31 Aug 2026).

survey.description: The Historic American Buildings Survey's WRITTEN historical and descriptive data for this building, quoted verbatim. It is text about the plates, not the plates: it states overall dimensions, storeys, bays, walls, chimneys, roof and openings as a surveyor recorded them, and it is a poor source for room dimensions, which live on the measured drawings (wp-9.2-what-the-tradition-actually-does.md §7 Q10). OCR is noisy -- a `4` reads as `h` -- so every figure taken from a quote is carried `as_printed` in `measurements`.

item.description: The Library's item id, e.g. va0433.

survey_no.description: The HABS number as the data page's own header prints it, e.g. VA-141.

prepared.description: Who wrote the data page and when, as it says.

field.description: Which part of the survey's own outline the quote comes from (Part II.B exterior: dimensions, foundations, walls, structural system, porches, chimneys, openings, roof; II.C interior: plan, stairways, finishes). These map onto the ontology's slots nearly one for one, which is why the survey is worth quoting.

text.description: Verbatim, OCR errors included. A contiguous span, never two spans joined with an ellipsis.

page.description: The page marker the data sheet prints (`HABS No. VA-141 (Page 2)`), or a statement that none was legible in the extract. A quote with no page cannot be checked against the sheet.

name.description: The corpus's measurement vocabulary where one fits (`overall_width_ft`, `wall_thickness_in`, `chimney_stack_count`); otherwise a plain name that says what it is.

as_printed.description: The figure exactly as the quote prints it, OCR noise included. The parse below is a reading of this string and may be wrong; this string is what was read.

rights_evidence.description: The rights statement AS THE SOURCE WORDS IT, verbatim. Not a conclusion. The Library of Congress says 'No known restrictions on images made by the U.S. Government; images copied from other sources may be restricted' on every HABS item alike -- byte-identical on a government photograph and on a HABS photograph OF somebody else's copyrighted drawing. A machine may record this sentence; it may not read a licence out of it. There is deliberately no `license` property in this schema.
